reconcile.connective: Commentators read "son of Zerah" as a telescoped genealogy — ben naming a remote ancestor while Carmi remains Achan's immediate father.

discrepancy.connective: The objection is catalogued by Steve Wells in the Skeptics Annotated Bible, who asks plainly whether Achan's father was Carmi (Josh 7:1) or Zerah (Josh 7:24; 22:20).

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (2013); contradiction "Who was Achan's father?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/achan.html)

excerpts.excerpt_text: Did not Achan the son of Zerah,.... One that descended from Zerah the son of Judah …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly glosses the bare "son of Zerah" of 22:20 as "one that descended from Zerah," i.e. a remote ancestor, dissolving the apparent father conflict with 7:1.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Judah had two sons by Tamar: Pharez and Zarah. Zarah was father of Zabdi, and Zabdi of Carmi, the father of Achan.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Lays out the full line — Zarah (Zerah) the ancestor, Carmi the immediate father — showing 7:1's chain and 7:24/22:20's shorthand describe the same man.

pd_work.resource: Adam Clarke, Commentary on the Bible (1832), on Joshua 7:1
pd_work.author: Adam Clarke
pd_work.note: Clarke spells out the genealogy (Zarah > Zabdi > Carmi > Achan) and the span between Achan and Zerah, treating this passage's father/ancestor question directly.

link.note: No allowlisted page treating this specific contradiction could be confirmed (GotQuestions' Achan/Zerah pages do not address the father-vs-ancestor discrepancy); link omitted rather than guessed.
